findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct or verify the claim that `rebar search --output json` is 'silently treated as a literal query term': the code path `_reject_unknown_option` already returns exit 2 with 'unknown option' for any unrecognized dashed token — restate the current behavior accurately (flag is entirely unrecognized/hard-rejected).
evidence: Plan claim: 'Passing `--output json` is silently treated as a literal query term, so it returns no matches and emits nothing parseable, which is its own small defect.'
src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py:489-495 — `elif arg.startswith('-'): return _reject_unknown_option(arg, ...)` for any unrecognized dashed token in _cmd_search
src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py:33-44 — _reject_unknown_option prints 'Error: unknown option' + usage and returns exit 2

src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py:113 — `_SEARCH_VALUE_OPTS = frozenset({'--status', '--type', '--has-tag', '--sort'})` does not include '--output', so --output is never coalesced with a following value
findings.finding: The plan asserts that passing `--output json` to `rebar search` is 'silently treated as a literal query term, so it returns no matches and emits nothing parseable, which is its own small defect.' The code refutes this: in `_cmd_search`, `--output` is not in `_SEARCH_VALUE_OPTS`, so it is not coalesced with its value, and any token starting with `-` that is unrecognized falls into `elif arg.startswith('-'): return _reject_unknown_option(...)`, which prints `Error: unknown option '--output'` plus usage and returns exit 2. So `--output json` today is a HARD usage error, not a silent no-match.
findings.location: Plan section 'The fix shape already exists on the sibling command' (final sentence); relates to AC line 'An unrecognized --output value is a hard error, not silently absorbed into the query string'
scenarios: Author writes/sizes a fix believing `--output json` currently degrades to a literal query term when in fact it already exits 2 with an error

AC line 'An unrecognized --output value is a hard error, not silently absorbed' may be partly satisfied already for the STRING '--output json' specifically (though a genuinely unrecognized --output VALUE like `--output=bogus` is a separate case once the flag is added)
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'Passing `--output json` is silently treated as a literal query term, so it returns no matches and emits nothing parseable' with an accurate description: `--output` is not a recognized search flag, so `rebar search --output json` currently exits 2 with 'Error: unknown option '--output''. Reframe the defect as 'search rejects the flag rather than supporting it', and keep AC5 (unrecognized --output VALUE is a hard error) for the post-implementation case.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the snippet mechanism: have the search matcher return the match offset/term span (or a bounded context window) alongside each matched state, and define snippet behavior for predicate-only / multi-term queries where there is no single free-text match.
evidence: reducer/search.py:78-84 computes `hay = _haystack(st)` and appends the whole state on match — no offset/context is retained
AC line: 'A match snippet (the matched term with surrounding context) is returned'
The sibling `list --output llm` (the stated consistency anchor) has no snippet concept, so 'behaves consistently with list --output llm' does not cover snippet mechanism
findings.finding: The match-snippet acceptance criterion introduces a projection field with no existing data-flow source: `search_states` (reducer/search.py) matches over a computed `_haystack` but returns only the matched state dicts, discarding the match position/offset. The plan names the snippet as a required output but does not specify how the matched term + surrounding context is captured and threaded from the matcher to the projection.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'A match snippet ... is returned so the caller can tell WHY a ticket matched'
scenarios: Implementer projects id/title/status but has no captured offset to build the snippet from, and must retrofit search_states to return match spans
Multi-term / predicate-only queries (e.g. status:open) have no free-text term to snippet — behavior unspecified
findings.suggested_fix: Extend `search_states` to return, per match, the matched term and a bounded char window around the first hit in the haystack (or None for predicate-only matches), and have the summary projection carry that as a `match`/`snippet` field.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the summary-projection schema explicitly: name the schema (reuse a restricted `ticket_state_llm` variant vs. a new `search_result` schema), enumerate its keys including the minified key for the match snippet, and reconcile the 'consistent with list --output llm' requirement (AC3) with the 'no desc/cm' requirement (AC1/AC2).
evidence: AC3: 'rebar search --output llm exists and behaves consistently with rebar list --output llm'
AC1: 'defaults to a summary projection … not full description or comment bodies'

src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state_llm.schema.json: keys include optional 'desc' (description) and 'cm' (comments) — the very fields AC1 says search must omit; this is the SSOT for every `--output llm` emitter via to_llm()
src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py: list/session-logs emit `to_llm(t)` — one shared llm shape
ABSENCE: plan names no schema id/key vocabulary for the search projection or the snippet field
findings.finding: The `--output llm` summary projection is a referenced structured-output schema whose value vocabulary is never defined, and it conflicts with the schema it must be 'consistent' with. `--output llm` is backed by the single SSOT schema `ticket_state_llm.schema.json` (TicketStateLLM), which permits the full-body keys `desc` (description) and `cm` (comments). AC3 requires `search --output llm` to 'behave consistently with `rebar list --output llm`' (same schema/shape), while AC1/AC2 require search to DROP description/comment bodies and ADD a match snippet. The plan never states whether search reuses TicketStateLLM, a restricted variant, or a new schema, nor what minified key the snippet takes in the key-map.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (AC1 summary projection, AC2 snippet, AC3 `--output llm` consistency)
scenarios: An implementer wires `search --output llm` to the existing `to_llm()`/TicketStateLLM and it re-emits desc/cm, silently violating AC1/AC2
An implementer invents a new schema but the MCP/CLI coverage guards fail because it is not registered in OUTPUT_SCHEMAS
findings.suggested_fix: State that search emits a new SSOT schema (e.g. `search_result.schema.json`) reusing common.schema.json enums, listing exactly id/a/ttl/t/st/pr plus a snippet key (e.g. `sn`), registered in OUTPUT_SCHEMAS; and clarify that `--output llm` consistency means 'same minified-key convention as list', not 'same full-body shape'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Bind the MCP search outputSchema to the SAME named canonical SSOT schema as the CLI summary projection (registered in OUTPUT_SCHEMAS), and state whether the match-snippet field appears in that schema so the coverage guards pass.
evidence: AC: 'The MCP search tool's outputSchema reflects the summary projection'

docs/output-schemas.md:173-184: MCP pydantic models mirror the SSOT schemas; every outputSchema-advertising tool is driven on a fixture store and validated, so 'a new MCP tool cannot ship an unvalidated outputSchema'
tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_output_schema_coverage.py: every outputSchema advertiser must map to a canonical shape or be a documented exemption
ABSENCE: plan does not name the canonical schema the search outputSchema mirrors, nor whether the snippet field is in that schema
findings.finding: The MCP search tool's outputSchema AC references a canonical schema/vocabulary that is never defined. MCP outputSchemas MIRROR a canonical JSON Schema registered in `OUTPUT_SCHEMAS`, and coverage guards forbid advertising an unvalidated schema. The AC 'reflects the summary projection' names no canonical schema, no field set, and does not address the snippet field's presence in the MCP model.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria: 'The MCP search tool's outputSchema reflects the summary projection'
scenarios: Implementer adds an MCP outputSchema for search that has no registered canonical schema → test_schema_coverage / test_mcp_output_schema_coverage fails
MCP outputSchema and CLI --output llm shape drift because the plan pinned neither to a shared SSOT schema

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the projection mechanism: state whether search's summary default reuses the existing `include_body`/`--full` body-drop seam (which list uses) vs. the orthogonal `--output llm` key-minifier (to_llm/shorten_comment, which RETAINS comment bodies), so the KB target is actually met.
evidence: _cmd_list carries `"include_body": False` with `--full` opting body back in (src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py:247-256)

TicketQuery.include_body default True, honored in reads.py:457 ('if not include_body' drops the bulky fields) — the actual body-dropping seam, exposed library-side as `full` (src/rebar/_lib_reads.py:165) and engine-side as include_body (src/rebar/_engine_support/ticket_query.py:52)

to_llm only remaps keys (src/rebar/reducer/llm_format.py:145-167) and shorten_comment abbreviates keys / drops timestamp but KEEPS the comment body (llm_format.py:84-93) — so `--output llm` does not by itself drop bodies
findings.finding: The plan frames `list --output llm` as the lean format to mirror for search, but leanness on `list` is actually delivered by a SEPARATE `--full`/`include_body` toggle, while `--output llm` (to_llm) is orthogonal key-minification that retains full comment bodies. Mirroring `--output llm` alone would not drop bodies; the directly-reusable projection toggle already threaded through the read stack is `include_body`.
findings.location: Plan sections 'The fix shape already exists on the sibling command' and AC3 ('rebar search --output llm exists and behaves consistently with rebar list --output llm')
scenarios: Implementer wires `search --output llm` to to_llm and finds comment bodies still emitted, missing the KB-not-hundreds-of-KB target (AC8)
Two divergent 'lean' mechanisms (include_body vs --output llm) drift apart between list and search
findings.suggested_fix: Base the search summary default on `include_body=False` (the seam already threaded through TicketQuery/_reads/_lib_reads), and treat `--output llm` as the existing key-minification layer applied on top — do not reimplement a third projection.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Acknowledge the search-default output change as a breaking change and state the migration path (e.g. explicit opt-in `--output full`/`--full` flag preserving old behavior, and note whether the JSON shape is versioned or if callers must migrate to `rebar show`).
evidence: '`rebar search` defaults to a summary projection: at minimum id, alias, title, type, status, and priority — not full `description` or `comment` bodies'
The current documented output is a JSON array carrying full `description` plus a `comments` array — any consumer relying on that shape breaks when the default changes.
findings.finding: Changing the default output of `rebar search` from full ticket bodies to a summary projection is a breaking change for any existing consumer (scripts, agents, MCP callers) that currently parses `description`/`comments` from search results, but the plan does not acknowledge the break or provide an expand-contract / rollback path.
scenarios: An existing script or the MCP search tool consumer that reads ticket bodies from `rebar search` output silently gets empty/absent body fields after the default flip.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a note under Acceptance Criteria that the default change is breaking, and pin the opt-in flag name that restores full bodies so consumers have a deterministic migration.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether `rebar list` projection changes are in-scope here or explicitly out-of-scope-and-tracked-in-a-named-follow-up, and remove the 'either/or'.
evidence: 'The same projection question is answered for `rebar list` (290 KB for `--status=open`), either here or in a linked ticket'
findings.finding: Acceptance criterion 6 defers a real scope decision to the executor via 'either here or in a linked ticket', which is a placeholder rather than a decision about whether `rebar list` projection work is in-scope for this ticket.
scenarios: Executor cannot tell whether shipping this ticket requires also fixing `rebar list` or merely filing a follow-up, changing the size and definition-of-done of the work.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one: fold `rebar list --output llm` parity into this ticket's ACs, OR state that a linked follow-up ticket owns it and remove AC 6 from this ticket's done-criteria.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that search routes its --output flag through the existing `parse_output`/`OutputFormatError` seam (as `list`/`show` do) so the hard-error (AC5) is reused, not reimplemented.
evidence: parse_output already raises OutputFormatError on an unknown value: 'unsupported output format ... Supported: ...' (src/rebar/_engine_support/output.py:124-127)

_cmd_show and _cmd_list both call parse_output (reads_cli.py:121, 230); _cmd_search parses argv by hand and never calls parse_output (reads_cli.py:472-497), which is exactly why --output leaks into the query
findings.finding: AC5 (unrecognized --output is a hard error) and the 'small defect' of --output being absorbed as a query term describe behavior the existing `parse_output` seam already provides via OutputFormatError; the root cause is that _cmd_search never calls parse_output. The plan should specify reusing that seam rather than adding bespoke --output handling to search.
findings.location: Plan section 'The fix shape already exists on the sibling command' ("Passing --output json is silently treated as a literal query term") and AC5
scenarios: Implementer writes new --output validation for search instead of routing through parse_output, duplicating the error contract and diverging from list/show
findings.suggested_fix: In _cmd_search, call parse_output(argv, "reader") first (as _cmd_list does) so --output llm/json is extracted and unknown values raise OutputFormatError before query parsing.
